items.prompt:
Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, strong readable silhouettes, deep near-black shadows. Light tells the story: a few strong sources — crystals and cracks that glow from within — throw colored light upward, the light comes from below. Cold and warm light contrast. Dust motes and grains of sand float in the light. Moderate detail, clean readable forms. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime. Match the brushwork, lighting and color handling of the attached style reference images, but do NOT copy their subjects, objects, letters or composition.

Format: game UI icon, square. One bold emblem, centered, about 80% of the canvas, frontal view, a simple strong silhouette that stays readable at 24 px, crisp clean edges, painted material detail inside the silhouette. The glow stays inside the shape: no halo outside the silhouette.

Subject: 'Rune of Valor', the emblem of a hero's valor. A thick rounded-hexagon tablet of dark basalt with a bevelled rim of old gold; carved deep into its face is a five-pointed star made of angular rune strokes, glowing warm gold (#DDBC7A) from within; hairline cracks in the stone leak the same golden light. Frontal, symmetric, heavy and precious.

Isolate the subject on a perfectly flat, uniform, solid pure magenta background (#FF00FF) that fills the whole canvas edge to edge: no gradient, no vignette, no texture, no floor, no cast shadow, no reflection, no glow or light spill on the background, no checkerboard transparency pattern. Leave a clear margin of background around the subject. Do not use magenta or similar colors anywhere in the subject.

No text, no letters, no numbers, no real-world alphabets, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no border or frame around the picture.

items.title: Арена боя · Мастерская форм, вид сверху
items.source: docs/gdd/08-биомы.md §8.5; docs/lore/мастерская-форм-текст.md, с. 2; docs/lore/дайджест.md «Мотивы и палитра»
items.prompt:
Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, strong readable silhouettes, deep near-black shadows. Light tells the story: a few strong sources — crystals and cracks that glow from within — throw colored light upward, the light comes from below. Cold and warm light contrast. Dust motes and grains of sand float in the light. Moderate detail, clean readable forms. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime. Match the brushwork, lighting and color handling of the attached style reference images, but do NOT copy their subjects, objects, letters or composition.

Format: vertical battle background for a phone screen, portrait 9:16. Strict top-down orthographic view, the camera looks straight down at the floor like a tabletop RPG battle map: no horizon, no perspective walls, no ceiling, no sky. The central area stays open, calm and lower in contrast: two teams of five cards will stand on it, heroes in the lower third and enemies in the upper third. Put the interesting details along the edges and in the corners. Even, readable lighting over the playfield, no strong hotspot in the center.

Subject: the floor of the Workshop of Forms, the first hall under the city of Endalor, where a god once sculpted living beings from clay and abandoned the work halfway. Large worn stone floor slabs with cracks; drifts and still ripples of pale sand everywhere; in the cracks grow white-green crystals glowing from within, their cold light pooling on the floor. Two or three columns of sand seen from above: thin streams fall from the unseen vault into round conical piles with a soft haze around them. Along the left and right edges: parts of heavy wooden worktables seen from above with unfinished clay works lying on them — a hand without fingers, a face without features, half of a small beast — sculpting chisels, clay-stained cloths, clay pots. At the very top and bottom edges: the foot of the stone walls with half-formed clay bodies emerging from the stone, made precisely and calmly, unfinished, not grotesque. Colors: near-black stone, cold white-green crystal light, pale sand, warm ochre clay as the only warm accent. No grid, no characters on the playfield.

No text, no letters, no numbers, no real-world alphabets, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no border or frame around the picture.
items.status: заменён: в первом промте Lite нарисовал слоты карт, Pro сделал зал тёплым; промт исправлен

items.prompt:
Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, strong readable silhouettes, deep near-black shadows. Subject: Ilmerra, an elven woman from long ago, keeper of a hall where the hourglasses of those who had no kin were kept; a healer of the Air school. She holds a small old hourglass with scratched glass close to her ear and listens to the sand inside, eyes half-closed. Layered druid robes of muted sage-green and grey linen, a woven shawl, a simple necklace of wooden beads; faint white-green wisps of wind curl around her sleeves (Air school). Background: a vast quiet hall among colossal tree roots in the heart of the elven forest; in niches between the roots stand rows of hourglasses, each one slightly different, dim; soft white-green light rises from below, sand motes drift in the air. She is lit from below by that white-green light, with a subtle rim light on her hair.

items.prompt:
Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, strong readable silhouettes, deep near-black shadows. Light tells the story: a few strong sources — crystals and cracks that glow from within — throw colored light upward, the light comes from below. Cold and warm light contrast. Dust motes and grains of sand float in the light. Moderate detail, clean readable forms. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime. Match the brushwork, lighting and color handling of the attached style reference images, but do NOT copy their subjects, objects, letters or composition.

Format: vertical battle background for a phone screen, portrait 9:16. Strict top-down orthographic view, the camera looks straight down at the floor like a tabletop RPG battle map: no horizon, no perspective walls, no ceiling, no sky. The central playfield — the middle 60% of the width, from 15% to 85% of the height — is plain floor only: stone slabs, sand ripples and fine cracks, calm and lower in contrast. No crystals, objects, markings, slots, frames, rectangles, cards, tokens or figures on the playfield: the game places its own pieces there later. Put the interesting details along the edges and in the corners. Even, readable lighting over the playfield, no strong hotspot in the center.

Subject: the floor of the Workshop of Forms, the first hall under the city of Endalor, where a god once sculpted living beings from clay and abandoned the work halfway. Large worn stone floor slabs with cracks; drifts and still ripples of pale sand. White-green crystals glowing from within grow only in the cracks along the edges and in the corners; their cold light spills onto the floor. In the corners: thin streams of sand fall from the unseen vault into small round piles with a faint haze, like hourglasses nobody turns. Along the left and right edges: parts of heavy wooden worktables seen from above with unfinished clay works lying on them — a hand without fingers, a face without features, half of a small beast — sculpting chisels, clay-stained cloths, clay pots. At the very top and bottom edges: the foot of the stone walls with half-formed clay bodies emerging from the stone, made precisely and calmly, unfinished, not grotesque. The hall is cold: near-black stone, white-green crystal light, pale sand. The only warm color is the ochre clay of the unfinished works. No candles, no fire, no warm lamps, no grid, no characters.

No text, no letters, no numbers, no real-world alphabets, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no border or frame around the picture.

Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, strong readable silhouettes, deep near-black shadows. Light tells the story: a few strong sources — crystals and cracks that glow from within — throw colored light upward, the light comes from below. Cold and warm light contrast. Dust motes and grains of sand float in the light. Moderate detail, clean readable forms. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime. Match the brushwork, lighting and color handling of the attached style reference images (approved game art), but do NOT copy their subjects, objects, letters or composition unless told to.

Format: vertical enemy card portrait, 4:5, shown small on the battle field (about 74 px wide) and large in the bestiary. The figure fills most of the frame, head and shoulders in the upper third, clear silhouette. The creature must follow the attached character reference exactly: shape, proportions, missing parts, clothing and tools. Render it in the painted style of the attached style reference. Background: the dim abandoned Workshop of Forms deep underground — dark stone, a thin stream of sand falling from a crack above, white-green crystals glowing from within in the cracks; darker and softer than the figure. Light comes from below; the clay is the only warm color in the scene.

Subject: 'The First Sketch', the boss of the last step of the Workshop — the very first attempt, begun and abandoned halfway. Huge, three times taller than a man, hunched, made of two halves that do not fit each other: the left half is an elf, the right half a beast — a shoulder in rough clay fur, an arm ending in a clawed paw, a beast's leg. Instead of a face a smooth mask with two hollows. A small foreign hand is stuck onto its side. It is not evil: it has been searching for a very long time for what to finish itself with. Show its scale — the figure barely fits the frame.

No text, no letters, no numbers, no real-world alphabets, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no border or frame around the picture.

items.source: docs/lore/мастерская-форм-текст.md, с. 14
items.prompt:
Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, strong readable silhouettes, deep near-black shadows. Light tells the story: a few strong sources — crystals and cracks that glow from within — throw colored light upward, the light comes from below. Dust motes and grains of sand float in the light. Moderate detail, clean readable forms. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime. Match the brushwork, lighting and color handling of the attached style reference images: the first shows how we paint characters, the second shows the Workshop's clay and its cold white-green crystal light. Do NOT copy their subjects or composition.

Format: vertical enemy card portrait, 4:5, shown small on the battle field (about 74 px wide) and large in the bestiary. Three-quarter view, the figure fills most of the frame, head and shoulders in the upper third, clear readable silhouette. This is a NEW ORIGINAL design made from the description only. World rule: every creature of the Workshop of Forms was sculpted of clay by a god and left unfinished — the 'samples' are rough unfinished tries, each named after its missing or unfinished part; the 'servants' are more finished, with even hands, faces, aprons and tools; the Master is the only finished one, smooth and polished. Everything is made precisely and calmly — unfinished, but not ugly and not grotesque. Clay colors: grey-green and warm ochre, visible finger marks and tool strokes on the clay. Figures have elven proportions unless the description says otherwise. Background: the dim abandoned Workshop of Forms deep underground — dark stone, a thin stream of sand falling from a crack above, white-green crystals glowing from within in the cracks; darker and softer than the figure. The whole scene is lit by cold white-green crystal light from below; no red, orange or warm light; the clay is the only warm color. All fourteen creatures of this set share the same painting style, palette and lighting. Every creature is made entirely of clay: a matte clay surface with finger marks, seams and tool strokes; no human skin, no realistic flesh; hair is sculpted clay; eyes are pressed hollows or smooth clay without pupils. They must not look like living people, orcs or goblins.

Subject: 'Prop', a servant of the Workshop: on servants like him the work was held in place while the clay set, and nobody has ever managed to move him. A broad, squat, immovable elf of grey-green clay with warm ochre patches — wide as a door, a thick neck, heavy shoulders, pointed elven ears, a calm stubborn face with pressed eyes. A clay apron, forearms bound in cloth wraps. He stands half-turned behind a thick stone slab that rests on the floor in front of him like a tower shield: one shoulder is braced against its top edge and both clay hands grip it. The slab covers only his lower body and one side; his head, broad shoulders, chest and both arms stay clearly visible above and around it. Carved on the slab is the sign of the Workshop — a simple hourglass outline, not letters and not a rune. The slab bears fresh chips and cracks from blows it has taken; dust and sand shake off it as if a blow has just landed, and he does not move. Behind him on a workbench stands a half-finished clay figure propped up with wooden struts — the work he once held while it set.

No text, no letters, no numbers, no runes that look like letters, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no border or frame around the picture. No gore, no blood, no horror grotesque.

items.title: Арена Эхо: Иш-Кантун, неделя эльфов — 21:9, одна сцена без перехода
items.source: ADR-0025, п. 8; ADR-0024; docs/content/герои/состав-героев.md, «Эльфы — Иш-Кантун»; раскладка — jobs/arena-02.json
items.prompt:
Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, strong readable silhouettes, deep near-black shadows. Light tells the story: a few strong sources — cracks and jade inlays in old stone that glow from within — throw colored light upward, the light comes from below. Cold and warm light contrast. Dust motes, pollen and tiny sparks float in the light. Moderate detail, clean readable forms. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime, no cartoon.

Format: wide horizontal battle background for a landscape phone screen, 21:9. Strict top-down orthographic view, the camera looks straight down at the ground like a tabletop RPG battle map: no horizon, no perspective, no side view of buildings, no sky. The attached image is our battle arena of a different place, the Workshop of Forms: take from it ONLY the straight-down camera, the scale, the layout of the zones and the painting style. Do NOT copy its objects, materials or colors: no worktables, no clay figures, no crystals, no sand. The game puts its cards along the left and right sides: five hero cards in the left quarter and five enemy cards in the right quarter, from the top edge to the bottom edge. So the left quarter (0-25% of the width) and the right quarter (75-100% of the width) must be open, flat, evenly lit ground over their whole height: plaza slabs, moss in the seams and fine cracks only — no steps, no walls, no statues, no bowls, no plants, no objects there. Unlike our biome arenas, this arena is a single scene: the fight begins and ends here, the camera never moves on to a next room, so nothing in the picture leads onward — no doorway, no road, no stairway, no passage out of the picture. The forest appears only as a thin dark strip along the very top and bottom edges, no more than 7% of the height. All details are placed only in the central half (25-75% of the width), close to the top and bottom edges; the middle of the central half stays calm and open, because the game shows banners there.

Subject: the great plaza of Ish-Kantun at night, at the foot of a jade stepped pyramid deep in an ancient forest, seen straight from above — the one place where the whole fight happens. Ground: large worn slabs of pale grey stone with a faint jade tint, tightly fitted, some lifted and cracked by roots; dark moss in the seams, a few fallen leaves and scattered green feathers; thin cracks glow from within with cold jade-green light. In the central half only: along the top edge, the lowest tiers of a jade-green stepped pyramid seen straight from above — straight parallel step edges running across the central half, cut off by the top edge of the picture; along the bottom edge, a great round stone calendar disc set flat into the plaza, seen straight from above, only its upper half visible, carved with concentric rings of abstract ornament — notches, spirals, feather and jaguar-spot patterns, nothing like writing or numbers — with jade-green light glowing in its grooves; near the pyramid and near the disc, two wide stone bowls of smoldering copal resin with warm amber embers and thin curls of pale smoke; a few black obsidian shards and jade beads on the slabs. Along the very top and bottom edges, giant dark forest leaves and roots crowd in over the edge as a thin strip. The plaza is cold: near-black shadows, jade-green light; the only warm color is the amber glow of the copal embers. No characters, no animals, no bodies, no cards, no grid.

No text, no letters, no numbers, no glyphs, no hieroglyphs, no real-world scripts, no carvings that look like writing or numerals, no occult symbols, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no border or frame around the picture. No gore, no blood, no skulls, no sacrifice, no horror grotesque.

items.prompt:
Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, strong readable silhouettes, deep near-black shadows. Light tells the story: a few strong sources — cracks and jade inlays in old stone that glow from within — throw colored light upward, the light comes from below. Cold and warm light contrast. Dust motes, pollen and tiny sparks float in the light. Moderate detail, clean readable forms. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime, no cartoon.

Enemy card portrait, 4:5, shown small on the battle field (about 74 px wide) and large in the bestiary. Camera at chest height, waist-up: the bottom edge of the picture cuts the body at the waist — head, torso and arms in frame, no hips, no legs; the legs are never visible, whatever the pose. The figure is centered and fills most of the frame; the head sits in the upper third with a little space above it. The body is turned in a three-quarter view toward the LEFT side of the picture, where its enemies stand; its weapon, its spell or the thing it is named after is thrust toward the left and clearly shown in front of the body. It is an enemy: dangerous, alive and caught in action — not a model posing, not a statue. Its story reads from its body, its pose and the place around it. World: these are the people of Ish-Kantun, an ancient, long-lived forest civilization of elves: jade stepped pyramids in a dark forest, cloaks and headdresses of feathers, obsidian blades, quilted cotton armor, jaguar pelts, great carved stone calendars; they counted their days in the circles of the Great Count, and when the circle ended they came out of the forest to take other people's breath and start the count anew. Their look is inspired by the ancient Maya, but they are clearly ELVES: tall and slender, long pointed ears, ageless narrow faces, warm bronze skin with dark painted patterns, heavy jade ear spools; they must not look like real-world people, orcs or goblins. Colors: muted and earthy, like all our enemies — deep jade green, dark bronze, bone white, obsidian black, dull old gold, a little faded red; everything else sinks into near-black shadow. Light, the same for the whole set: night; the light comes from below — cold jade-green light glowing from within cracks and jade inlays in old stone rises onto the figure; crisp cold rim light on its edges; a small warm amber glow of embers is the only warm light. Background: its own place in Ish-Kantun, darker and softer than the figure, with depth. All fifteen portraits of this set share the same framing, painting style, palette and lighting.

The enemy: the Feathered Archer, a rank-and-file archer of Ish-Kantun. A lean young elf with long pointed ears, long black hair tied up with bunches of dark green and grey feathers, a stripe of dark green paint across his eyes, a simple cotton wrap and a collar of bone beads; on his back a quiver of arrows fletched with the same feathers, and more feathers hang from the quiver. Action: he shoots from the foliage where no one can see him — half-hidden among giant dark leaves, only his face, arms and bow come out of them; he draws a long bow to full draw and aims to the left, the arrowhead a black obsidian point; his narrowed eyes are fixed on a target to the left. A breath of wind (Air) stirs the feathers and the leaves around him. Background: the dense night canopy of the forest of Ish-Kantun, huge leaves and hanging lianas; far below behind him, the dim shape of a stepped pyramid with a jade-green glow at its base.

No text, no letters, no numbers, no glyphs, no hieroglyphs, no real-world scripts, no carvings that look like writing or numerals, no occult symbols, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no border or frame around the picture. No gore, no blood, no skulls, no sacrifice, no horror grotesque.

items.source: ADR-0027 — цвет: фиолетовая; форма — огранённая капля по образцу автора, описан словами (ADR-0012); GDD §3.1 — семь редкостей
items.prompt:
Dark fantasy game art with a menacing, gloomy, mystical atmosphere. Digital painting with soft transitions, elaborate shadows and an artistic emphasis on details. Lighting effects bring it to life: magical glow, aura and embers, light that comes from inside the subject and from below. Rich worn materials: dark forged iron, old gold, weathered stone, carst crystals glowing from within. Precious, dramatic, high contrast.

Format: game UI icon of a rarity, square, no border around the picture. One carst crystal — the magic crystal of this world — upright, centered, floating in the dark, about 80% of the canvas high. The crystal floats on pitch black: everything around it is solid pure black to the very edges of the canvas, never white or grey. All seven rarity icons are one series with one crystal shape: a faceted crystal drop, almond-like — full and rounded in its lower part, tapering to a point at the top, about two thirds as wide as it is tall — so that even at 24 px it reads as a solid spot of color. Its surface is cut into facets that lie like cells, with soft painterly edges; fine cracks run along the facets; a bright light rim runs along the whole contour. Energy of its own lives inside the crystal. The seven rarities form a ladder of inner light: the higher the rarity, the more light pours from inside. A bare crystal: no setting, no metal caps or bands, no stand, no base, no shards or sparks floating outside it. All the detail lives inside the silhouette. No runes, glyphs or symbols.

Rarity: Epic, the fourth of seven. A violet crystal: inside it, crystalline cells — a honeycomb of inner facets — catch a steady violet light.

The background is solid pure black (#000000), flat, edge to edge: no gradient, no texture, no floor, no cast shadow, no vignette, no checkerboard. Any glow stays close to the subject and fades into the black within a short distance. The whole icon with its glow fits inside the central 80% of the canvas in both width and height: an empty black margin of at least a tenth of the canvas stays on every side — top, bottom, left and right.

No text, no letters, no numbers, no real-world alphabets, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements.
